title: Social Media Can Suppress or Fuel Misinformation at Its Source, Depending on Civic Engagement
abstract: arXiv:2506.16355v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Social media is widely viewed as a channel for spreading misinformation, but its effects may begin earlier, by shaping whether misinformation is produced in the first place. We examine whether social media suppresses or amplifies the supply of misinformation and identify civic engagement as a key boundary condition. Using data on the GDP reporting of Chinese local governments from 2011 to 2019, we find that social media adoption reduces GDP misreporting only when civic engagement is high. This reduction is driven by posts that disclose specific economic data rather than promotional content. When civic engagement is low, however, social media adoption instead increases GDP misreporting. These findings reveal a dual upstream role of social media in the misinformation process: it can deter misinformation at its source when disclosures are exposed to engaged citizens, but can amplify its supply when civic engagement is limited.

translated_title: 社交媒体能够在源头抑制或助长错误信息，这取决于公民参与度
translated_abstract: 社交媒体被广泛视为传播错误信息的渠道，但其影响可能开始得更早——即塑造错误信息最初是否被生产出来。我们研究了社交媒体究竟是抑制还是放大错误信息的供给，并将公民参与度确定为一个关键的边界条件。利用2011年至2019年中国地方政府GDP上报的数据，我们发现只有当公民参与度较高时，社交媒体的采用才会减少GDP虚报。这种减少是由披露具体经济数据的帖子而非宣传性内容所驱动的。然而，当公民参与度较低时，社交媒体的采用反而会增加GDP虚报。这些发现揭示了社交媒体在错误信息过程中的双重上游角色：当信息披露面对有参与度的公民时，社交媒体可以在源头遏制错误信息的产生；但当公民参与度有限时，它则会放大错误信息的供给。
tldr: 该研究利用2011–2019年中国地方政府GDP数据发现，社交媒体对错误信息的影响始于源头：公民参与度高时社交媒体的采用会减少GDP虚报，参与度低时反而会增加虚报。
en_tdlr: Using Chinese local government GDP data from 2011–2019, this study shows that social media deters misinformation at its source—reducing GDP misreporting—only when civic engagement is high, but amplifies misreporting when civic engagement is low.
